mainEntity.name: How much does it cost to replace a Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 engine?

acceptedAnswer.text: Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 engine replacement costs range from £1,800 for used M275 units to £6,500 for fully rebuilt engines with 12-month warranty. Typical reconditioned M275 V12 prices sit between £3,200-£5,500 supply-only. Prices vary by engine code (M275 E55 vs M275 KE55), year, and whether supply & fit is included.

mainEntity.name: What are the signs of M275 V12 coil pack failure in an SL600?

acceptedAnswer.text: The most common symptom of M275 V12 coil pack failure in the Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 is a persistent misfire, often affecting cylinders 2-7 on the inner bank. Check engine light, rough idle, loss of power, and unburnt fuel smell from the exhaust are all warning signs. If ignored, misfires can destroy catalytic converters.

mainEntity.name: Is it worth replacing the engine in a Mercedes Benz SL600 V12?

acceptedAnswer.text: Replacing a Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 M275 V12 engine costs £3,200-£6,500 rebuilt, often representing better value than selling a depreciated V12 SL with engine faults. For low-mileage examples or collector-grade R230 SL600 V12s with full history, engine replacement preserves significant investment value.

mainEntity.name: What engine code is in my Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 and how do I check?

acceptedAnswer.text: Your Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 engine code appears on the engine block stamping, vehicle registration document, or via DVLA lookup using your registration number. Pre-facelift (2003-2006) SL600 V12s carry the M275 E55 (275.951), while facelift (2006-2011) models use the M275 KE55 (275.954).

mainEntity.name: Do Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 engines use timing chains or belts?

acceptedAnswer.text: The Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 M275 engine uses a duplex roller timing chain, not a belt. However, timing chain tensioner wear has been documented on higher-mileage examples, causing cold-start rattle. If ignored, chain stretch can lead to catastrophic engine damage.

historyTimeline.h2: Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 - Engine History & Specs at a Glance
historyTimeline.intro: The Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 represented the pinnacle of R230 grand touring refinement, pairing the flagship M275 twin-turbo V12 with Active Body Control suspension. Across its production life, the SL600 V12 received two distinct M275 engine variants - the 5.5L biturbo in pre-facelift cars and a higher-output version for facelift models.

milestones.description: **2003** - R230 SL600 V12 launches with M275 E55 5.5L V12 biturbo, 493hp, 800Nm
**2006** - R230 facelift introduces revised M275 KE55 5.5L V12 biturbo, 517hp, 830Nm, with updated engine management
**2008** - SL600 V12 continues with M275 KE55 through to end of R230 production
**2011** - R230 SL600 V12 production ends; no R231 SL600 variant produced

historyTimeline.closingNote: Every engine fitted to the Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 is covered below, with UK rebuilt pricing and known failure points.

commonProblems.h2: Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 Engine Problems - Repair Cost vs Replacement
commonProblems.h3: The Mercedes Benz SL600 V12's M275 twin-turbo engine delivers effortless V12 performance, but heat-related component failures - particularly ignition coil packs on the inner bank - frequently trigger urgent replacement searches. Every rebuilt M275 engine supplied through EnginesMarket includes upgraded coil packs and reinforced wiring, backed by a minimum 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty. Use the cost breakdown below to make an informed repair versus replacement decision for your R230 SL600 V12.

problems.h4: M275 V12 Ignition Coil Failure - Why SL600 V12 Misfires Cascade
problems.affectedModels: Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 (M275 E55 / M275 KE55, 2003-2011)
problems.rootCause: Extreme heat soak in the tightly packed V12 engine bay degrades ignition coil insulation, particularly on the inner bank cylinders. Failed coils cause persistent misfires, unburnt fuel washdown, and rapid catalytic converter poisoning. A leaking valve cover gasket can also allow oil into spark plug wells, destroying the coil PCB.

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Replacement of all 12 ignition coils with upgraded units, premium spark plugs, wiring harness inspection, ECU fault code clearance
repairOptions.longevity: Preventative solution at 60k miles. Stops catalytic converter damage and restores smooth idle

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Misfire tracing, oxygen sensor replacement, catalytic converter health check, fuel system pressure validation
repairOptions.longevity: Required if misfires have persisted over 2k miles. Identifies secondary damage before it worsens

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete V12 engine swap with specialist rebuilt long block, upgraded coil packs, reinforced wiring, bench-tested performance match, 12-month warranty
repairOptions.longevity: Recommended for severe cylinder scoring, hydrolock, or extensive internal washdown damage

problems.vehicleValueCheck: A typical 2006-2011 Mercedes Benz SL600 V12 currently values between £7,500 and £16,000 in the UK used market. With the rebuilt engine cost at £4,500-£6,500 supply-only (plus £900-£1,300 for fitment), replacement is financially viable for most examples. However, if your SL600 V12 is valued under £8,000, evaluate whether a used engine or targeted coil pack repair offers better value before committing to a full rebuild.
problems.recommendation: Replacing all 12 coils proactively at 60k miles prevents expensive catalytic damage. However, if misfires have already caused cylinder scoring or excessive oil dilution, a specialist rebuilt M275 V12 with upgraded coil packs and wiring harnesses delivers superior reliability. For SL600 V12 owners with confirmed coil-related misfires, we recommend immediate coil pack replacement and a catalytic converter health check before considering a full engine replacement.
problems.cta: -> Compare rebuilt M275 V12 engine prices for your Mercedes Benz SL600 V12

problems.h4: ABC Hydraulic Pump Misdiagnosis - Why SL600 V12 Engines Are Flagged as Failed
problems.rootCause: The Active Body Control hydraulic pump accumulators lose nitrogen pressure and internal seals fail, causing the ECU to trigger limp mode and rough idle. This electrical load spike and vacuum fluctuation is frequently misdiagnosed as internal engine damage by generic OBD scanners.

repairOptions.tier: Minor - Full ABC System Diagnostic & Pressure Check
repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Hydraulic pressure testing, accumulator nitrogen recharge, fault code tracing (C1525/C1526), ECU reset
repairOptions.longevity: Essential first step. Confirms whether drivability issues are suspension-related rather than engine-fault

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Pump seal replacement, accumulator rebuild, hydraulic fluid flush, system pressure validation
repairOptions.longevity: Restores proper suspension function and eliminates false engine misfire/limp mode triggers

repairOptions.whatItInvolves: Complete engine removal and replacement based on incorrect fault diagnosis
repairOptions.longevity: Strongly discouraged unless internal mechanical damage is independently verified

problems.recommendation: We strongly advise verifying ABC pump pressure codes (C1525/C1526) before pursuing engine work on your SL600 V12. A specialist hydraulic pump rebuild with upgraded seals typically restores drivability for under £2,000, avoiding unnecessary V12 engine replacement costs entirely.
